sentences.text: Hulsanpes was a dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur belonging to the family Dromaeosauridae.

The only known species is Hulsanpes perlei, named by Halszka Osmólska in 1982. The generic name means "foot of Khulsan," combining the Latinized locality name with the Latin word for foot, while the specific name honors the Mongolian paleontologist Altangerel Perle.
The species is based on the holotype specimen ZPAL MgD-I/173, which consists of a partial right foot and a brain fragment from an apparently immature individual.

The holotype includes a partial braincase fragment and a right metatarsus with three pedal phalanges. The roughly textured bones indicate it was likely a post-hatchling chick, and the preserved portion of the braincase measures just 1 cm in length.
The foot contains the second, third, and fourth metatarsals, plus the first and partial second phalanx of the second toe. The longest bone, the third metatarsal, measures 39 millimeters in length.
Hulsanpes remains were discovered in 1970 at Khulsan in the Gobi Desert during a Polish-Mongolian expedition and formally described in 1982 by Halszka Osmólska.

Researchers identified subcursorial adaptations for Hulsanpes, suggesting it may have had a more terrestrial lifestyle despite evidence that it likely spent much of its time in aquatic environments like rivers, swimming using both forelimbs and hindlimbs.

In 2017, Hulsanpes was placed in the new clade Halszkaraptorinae alongside Halszkaraptor and Mahakala. Hulsanpes represents the first known record of the basal dromaeosaurid subfamily Halszkaraptorinae. In 2018, Cau and Madzia confirmed Hulsanpes as a valid taxon and the oldest record of the subfamily Halszkaraptorinae. The parent group of Hulsanpes is Halszkaraptorinae.

Hulsanpes lived in what is now Asia during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage. The time range for Hulsanpes is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago. The environment included large rivers, other water bodies, and prominent dune-like terrains.
Hulsanpes shared its habitat with dinosaurs including Bagaceratops, Gobipteryx, Parvicursor, Saichania, Tarchia, and Tylocephale.
